The Revenue Marketing Content Gap

Revenue marketing teams invest heavily in useful research, but static assets make it difficult to understand which ideas actually move a buying group forward.

The benchmark found that 42 percent of buyers revisit a useful resource before they invite another stakeholder into the evaluation.

Why campaign content stalls

A single download hides the reading path, the questions a buyer explored, and the proof that earned attention. This leaves demand generation teams with a form fill instead of an engagement narrative.

Teams should turn one source into an ordered sequence of findings, examples, and next-step choices so buyers can explore the argument at their own pace.

What a connected journey reveals

A guided experience can measure chapter views, resource opens, decision-path selections, dwell time, and CTA intent while preserving the source argument.

Customer research shows that marketing and revenue leaders use these signals to tailor follow-up and help sellers focus on the questions a buying group is already asking.

A practical launch sequence

Start with the premise, let buyers choose a relevant question, attach source-backed proof, and end with one explicit next action. Every claim should retain a citation to the original source.

Recommended source-to-experience sequence
StageBuyer action
PremiseUnderstand why the topic matters
ProofInspect evidence and examples
Next stepRequest a working session
